Delivery Hero treats the pre-August 2021 model risk as probable and the post-August 2021 model risk as possible only.

- For the model operated by Glovo Spain until August 2021, the risk is more likely than not to materialize, so appropriate provisions are recognized in the Consolidated Financial Statements [4].
- For the model in place since August 2021, the rider risk is deemed possible but not probable, so it is disclosed as a contingency — a contingent liability of €440 to 770 million for the ongoing social security investigation [2][4].
- For the pre-2021 proceedings, Glovo had to provide bank guarantees to Spanish courts in 2024 to secure payment of the liabilities claimed by the authorities [1][3].
- Glovo decided to progressively move to an employment-based model in Spain to avoid further legal uncertainties regarding the model in place since August 2021 [1].
- Glovo received preliminary reclassification decisions from local authorities in January 2025, will defend the self-employed status through all available instances, and will continue cooperating with the Spanish authorities [1].

Zalando - end of 2022: EUR 304.3m committed to fulfilment centres
Zalando - end of 2024: 59.5m EUR committed to fulfilment centres

The commitment fell by 304.3 − 59.5 = 244.8m EUR between the end of 2022 and the end of 2024.
Approximately 850,000 riders delivered at least one order for Delivery Hero in 2024.

In 2024, Zalando evolved Zalando Plus by introducing a points-based system to reward customer loyalty, replacing the previous model. Points are earned through purchases and other activities such as subscribing to newsletters, and unlock four distinct benefit levels with perks like birthday vouchers and exclusive events. The new free-to-join model was initially tested in Spain and then expanded to France and Austria, with further rollout planned for 2025 (combined management report, Group strategy; Accounting policies).

At year-end, the report mentions increased accruals for the reimbursement of Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers at the beginning of 2025, which are included in "others" within other current non-financial liabilities (Notes 9.–26.).

Turkcell - 2G licence extension (2023): EUR 120 million (plus EUR 21.6 million of value-added taxes); paid in instalments — initial payment of EUR 81.6 million (down payment plus VAT) paid in Turkish Lira at TRY 1.7 billion during 2023, approximately half of the remaining installments amounting to EUR 31.1 million paid in April 2024 at TRY 1.1 billion, with the remaining amount to be paid within a year.
Vodafone Turkey - 2G licence extension (2023): €120 million for a six-year extension until 30 April 2029 (excluding 18% VAT); paid the extension fee in advance with a capital injection, signing the extension agreement effective as of 27 April 2023.

Both operators agreed to the same headline extension fee of EUR 120 million, but Turkcell is paying in instalments (partly in Turkish Lira), whereas Vodafone Turkey paid its fee in advance via a capital injection.
